differences.what: Circle centre: old polylabel centre; current vertex average of the contact polygon.
Circle radius: old = polylabel inscribed radius x shift (0.95 default, relative); current = shift used as an absolute radius (circle_radius, 20 mm default). Different meaning and different default.

Circle orientation and phase: old x-axis = direction of the polygon edge closest to the centre (orient_to_closest_edge=true), y = cross(x, plane normal), points at angles 45 + i*(360/n) degrees with INTEGER division 360/n (e.g. n=7 gives 51 deg steps and an open gap); current x = get_fast_plane().x_axis(), y = z x x, angles 2*pi*i/n, no 45 deg offset.
Point count: old passes division_length as int `division` unclamped; current clamps to 1..100 and collapses to a single centre point when radius < 1e-9 or n <= 1.

Kernel already provides Polyline::polylabel_circle_division_points(division_direction_in_3d, polylines, division=4, scale=0.75, precision=1.0, orient_to_closest_edge=true), the exact old signature; the builder does not call it.
Per-point output layout (2 lines per point per face, drill types) matches the old loop.

No kernel equivalent of inscribe_rectangle_in_convex_polygon seen in polyline.h (only bounding_rectangle, quick_hull, polylabel, grid_of_points_in_polygon); a port needs a new kernel routine or a wood-side one (searched only polyline.h; other kernel headers unverified).
Defaults: spacing 30 vs 6; shift 0.5 vs 0.95 and not exposed; old shift is a scale (0..1), not an offset.

differences.what: Old builds m[0]/m[1] from MALE[i]/MALE[i+1] (each twice) and f[0]/f[1] from FEMALE[i]/FEMALE[i+1] (each twice) with type nothing, and unlike tt_e_p_0..5 leaves orient=true so the unit-box geometry IS oriented to the connection volumes. Nothing of this exists in the port; every other family has a *_custom factory (ss_e_ip/ss_e_op/ts_e_p/ss_e_r/cr_c_ip/b).

Also absent from the top-top dispatch: old case 48 -> side_removal(jo, elements) and old default -> tt_e_p_0 for any other id in 40..49. Current build_toptop returns false for 46..49 and build_family_default has no family-4 entry ('tt_e_p has none'), so an unknown id in family 40 produces no geometry instead of tt_e_p_0.

family.insertion_direction: The family has no insertion vector of its own; both old and current derive the drill axis from the FIRST joint volume rectangle: dir0 = unitize(joint_volumes[0][1] - joint_volumes[0][2]), dir1 = -dir0, then dir0 *= thickness(v0 = element_a, male), dir1 *= thickness(v1 = element_b, female); female lines = {p, p + dir0}, male lines = {p, p + dir1} (old 351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_joint_lib.cpp:5522-5534; current tt_e_p_drills.h:22-36,57-64). The type-40 volume is built in face_to_face: rect = bounding rectangle of the joint area; n = unitized (insertion_vectors0[i] if given, else the normal of element 0's contact face i: old Plane0[i].orthogonal_vector(), current el0.planes[i].z_axis()); copy A = rect moved by -n * dist(plane i, its opposite face plane of element 0) = -n*t0, copy B = rect moved by +n*t1; joint_volumes[0] = {A0, A1, B1, B0, A0}, joint_volumes[1] = {A3, A2, B2, B3, A3}, both extended by JOINT_VOLUME_EXTENSION[0]/[1] (old 351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_main.cpp:1150-1212; current src/joinery_solver/wood_algorithms/wood_feature_detection.cpp:875-941). Hence [1]-[2] = A1-B1 = -n*(t0+t1), so dir0 = -n (into element 0 from the contact plane, opposite to face i's normal / the given insertion vector) and dir1 = +n (into element 1). So the exploded-picture direction for target 0 (element_a) is -n * thickness_a and for target 1 (element_b) +n * thickness_b, with n the contact-face normal of element_a; the old merge step that would have re-clipped the drill lines against the element planes is disabled by an unconditional `continue` (351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_element.cpp:39-41), so the lines are exactly those lengths. In the JointPlate::orient(contact, elements) path the volumes come from contact->volumes[k] copied into connection.joint_volumes[k] (wood_element_joint_plate.cpp:705-707); that compute_face_contact fills them with the same top_top rectangles is stated by wood_session.h:116 ('plate contacts include joinery volumes') but the body was not read (unverified).

Cross-family facts worth flagging: (1) old group-4 defaults division_length=6, shift=0.95, default id 40 are reproduced in the solver table PARAMETER_DEFAULTS (joint_plate.cpp:438-440) but NOT by the factories, whose defaults are spacing 30 / shift 0.5 / circle_radius 20 absolute. (2) The enum values of hole and edge_insertion are swapped between old wood_cut.h (edge_insertion=1, hole=2) and current FabricationType (hole=1, edge_insertion=2); drill is 15 in both, so tt_e_p is unaffected but any numeric round-trip of other families is. The WoodSession::add_interaction body that the example calls (examples/elements/element_joint_plate_tt_e_p.cpp:50-51) was not located (Bash died on a full temp quota midway; Read-only search of wood_session.cpp 1100-1420,1522-1717 did not contain it), so whether a JointPlate interaction reaches host_drills, and how Plate / merge_features treat 2-point drill outlines, is UNVERIFIED; wood_element_plate.cpp has no occurrence of 'drill' (grep before the outage). (5) Old 'drill-line correction' against the element planes is dead code (continue at wood_element.cpp:41), so 2024 output lines are exactly thickness-long. (6) Docs: docs/elements/element_joint_plate.md:84-90 and the parameter table at 102-104 describe tt_e_p_3..5 as 'a grid at a spacing', which matches 2024 for _4/_5 only, not the current boundary-division builders.
